types.name: The Steady Compass
types.signature: You keep the room oriented when the talk turns.
types.room: You steady a conversation without taking it over.

types.name: The Silk Thread Connector
types.signature: You draw a fine line between people who belong in the same sentence.
types.room: You make the introduction that still matters a year later.

types.name: The Empire Architect
types.signature: You see the structure long before the room does.
types.room: You turn a scattered hour into a shape people can feel.

types.name: The Champagne Spark
types.signature: You arrive, and the hour lifts.
types.room: You raise the temperature of a quiet corner.

types.name: The Restless Polymath
types.signature: You follow a thought across every border it tries.
types.room: You join a practical point to a poem and make both clearer.

types.name: The Quiet Connoisseur
types.signature: You notice the detail everyone else talks over.
types.room: You let quality speak, and you do not rush it.

types.name: The Gilded Raconteur
types.signature: You give a story its proper light.
types.room: You hold a story until the room is ready for the ending.

types.name: The Velvet Provocateur
types.signature: You ask the question that makes the evening braver.
types.room: You disagree beautifully, and the room is better for it.

types.name: The Midnight Philosopher
types.signature: You stay for the thought that only arrives late.
types.room: You wait until the noise drops, then say the lasting thing.

questions.prompt: The room has just gone quiet.

answers.text: You let the silence finish its work.
You ask the thing everyone was circling.
You offer a story that belongs in the quiet.

questions.prompt: A new guest is standing just outside the talk.

answers.text: You draw them into the right conversation.
You make the first minute feel easy.
You wait until you know where they will be happiest.

questions.prompt: Someone describes a plan that is almost beautiful.

answers.text: You can see the structure it still needs.
You name the other field it belongs to.
You point to the one detail that would make it true.

questions.prompt: The hour is getting late, and the talk is getting better.

answers.text: You stay. The good thought is still on its way.
You keep the lift in the room.
You make sure no one is lost on the way there.

questions.prompt: Two people should know each other, and do not.

answers.text: You introduce them with the reason already in the sentence.
You see what they could build together.
You introduce the disagreement they will enjoy.

questions.prompt: A subject you love comes up, and you know a great deal.

answers.text: You open a second door into it.
You tell it so the room can feel it.
You follow it down to the question underneath.

questions.prompt: The conversation has become too agreeable.

answers.text: You offer the braver objection.
You bring it back to what people actually meant.
You change the air without scolding it.

questions.prompt: You are asked what you pay attention to.

answers.text: Quality, and the patience it asks for.
Almost everything, until it connects.
How separate efforts become one thing.

questions.prompt: A story in the room needs a teller.

answers.text: You give it shape, and an ending.
You tell it lightly, and leave people warmer.
You tell only the part that is exact.
You ask about the structure, not the noise.
You ask who it is for, and whether they are with it.
You ask what it refuses to be.

questions.prompt: The evening ends. What stays with you.

answers.text: The sentence that arrived last.
The people who should meet again.
The sudden brightness of the hour.
